content.thinking: Since clock locking isn't available on this rented card, I'll use a proxy test instead: forcing all table reads to a single row so they hit L1 and L2 table traffic disappears, revealing whether table traffic has any cost on this bench. I'll also use this same probe to compare s-tile-major versus bh-major ordering in the persistent kernel.

The proxy test shows table traffic does cost performance, with removal speeding up r0 by 3-4% at 64 threads and 7-10% at 256 threads, though the persistent kernel still lags ~8% due to its structure; bh-major ordering confirms s-tile-major isn't the culprit. Next, I'll force 4 CTAs/SM with `__launch_bounds__(256,4)` and run the full test with the persistent path limited to the M band.
